title: Subject pronouns in sentences
summary: Learn when a olla sentence can omit a subject pronoun and when it should remain explicit.
objectives: Recognise person from first- and second-person verb endings.
Omit an optional first- or second-person subject carefully.
Keep third-person subjects clear when context does not identify them.

sections.title: Some endings already name the person
paragraphs: In Finnish, minä, sinä, me, and te can be omitted when the verb ending makes the subject clear. Olen täällä still means “I am here”.
Keeping these pronouns is also grammatical. This lesson practises the shorter option when the instruction asks for it.
keyPoints: olemme and olette identify plural persons

sections.title: Third person needs a clear subject
paragraphs: The forms on and ovat do not name a specific person or group. If no earlier context identifies the subject, write hän or he.
This pack keeps third-person pronouns explicit in independent beginner sentences.
keyPoints: hän on in an independent sentence
he ovat in an independent sentence
context can change pronoun needs in longer texts

steps: The ending in olen identifies first-person singular.
The ending in olette identifies te.
The subject may be omitted when the addressee is clear.

examples.english: He or she is at school.
steps: On is third person but does not identify who.
Keep hän because no earlier context names the person.

commonMistakes: Do not assume every Finnish subject can disappear.
Pronoun omission is valid in writing when the verb ending makes the subject clear.
Follow the exercise instruction when it requests the shorter or explicit form.
